item.title: [Podcast] UN General Assembly: Reform, Rivalries and Trump’s Shadow
item.description:
It’s that time of year again when world leaders descend on New York for the United Nations’ annual General Assembly. In this special podcast episode, Dulcie Leimbach, editor-in-chief of PassBlue, and Paula Dupraz-Dobias, journalist at Geneva Solutions, sit down to discuss some of the critical issues at stake for the multilateral organization.
The General Assembly will hold its high-level week starting Tuesday, Sept. 22, where world leaders will tackle a packed agenda from conflicts to climate change to pandemic preparedness against a backdrop of growing discord between members and pressures on the multilateral system. As tradition requires, Donald Trump is scheduled to speak as the second head of state after Brazil on Tuesday, ahead of most of the other 193 member states.

item.title: Yemen escalation displaces more than 57,000 children: UNICEF
item.description: Renewed fighting in Yemen is deepening an already severe humanitarian crisis in a country where more than 12 million children depend on aid, after more than a decade of conflict.

item.title: As freshwater reserves shrink, countries must prepare for a new water reality
item.description: The world is entering a period in which abnormal water supplies are becoming the norm, with river flows, groundwater and glaciers all showing signs of sustained disruption, the UN weather agency warned on Thursday.

item.title: US likely committed war crimes against Iranian civilians: Independent experts
item.description: Independent investigators appointed by the UN’s Human Rights Council found “reasonable grounds” to believe that the United States committed war crimes during “indiscriminate attacks” against an Iranian school and residential area.

item.title: Guterres calls for action as hate speech spreads across new platforms online
item.description: The UN Secretary-General has called for concerted action by governments, technology companies and civil society to stamp out hate speech, emphasizing that “its toxic message is spreading fast and striking deep”.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Syria’s transition in the spotlight
item.description: While Syria is making progress in its political transition, the Security Council is meeting to hear briefings and discuss the situation on the ground, including recent reports of deadly armed clashes with an ISIS-affiliate terrorist group in the south and protests over rising fuel prices.

item.title: World News in Brief: Winter aid for Gaza, West Bank; Haiti food production; migrant deaths at sea; human rights funding
item.description: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) is seeking to raise $97.5 million to protect 540,000 children and their families in Gaza and the West Bank from harsh winter conditions in the coming months.

item.title: Gender equality woefully off track, new UN report reveals
item.description: At the current rate of progress, gender equality would take 171 years to achieve, a new UN report finds as institutions built to advance gains are being defunded and demobilised.
